Documentation › The desktop

Dock

Favorites and open apps, windows, Launchpad, minimized windows and the Trash

#What's in it

  • Launchpad (the grid icon): every app.
  • Pinned apps, then open apps that aren't pinned. One mark under an icon for each open window (up to three): a dot, and a short bar in your accent color for the window you're in. A minimized window keeps its app's icon and is listed as Minimized when you rest the pointer on it; clicking brings it back.
  • Show open apps (Settings → Desktop & Dock → Dock) can be turned off: the dock then holds only what you pinned, and the top bar's window buttons are the one list of what is open. The marks under pinned apps stay.
  • Trash: click to open; right-click for Empty Trash. Drop files on it and they go there, recoverable until you empty it.

#Using it

Click
Starts the app, or brings its window forward (a click on the window in front minimizes it); with several windows, each click brings the next one forward.
Middle-click
Starts another window of the app.
Rest the pointer
On an app with several windows, shows them; click one to pick it.
Right-click
The app's windows, New Window, the app's own actions (for example a new private window), and Keep in Dock / Remove from Dock.
Drag
Reorders pinned apps. To pin an app that isn't open, right-click it in Spotlight → Keep in Dock.
Drop a file on an app
Opens it with that app: drag one or more files out of Files or off the desktop and onto an icon, which lights up when it can take them. An app whose command accepts no file (a terminal, for instance) doesn't light up and doesn't take the drop. Dropped on the Trash, the files are moved there. If the dock is hidden, carrying files to the screen's edge brings it up, and it stays up until you let go.

#Style

Settings → Desktop & Dock → Dock → Style:

Floating
The default: one rounded shelf of frosted glass, held off the screen's edge.
Islands
The same shelf split in three pills of glass — Launchpad, your apps, the Trash — with a gap between them, as the top bar does in its floating style. The gap replaces the hairline before the Trash; the one between pinned and open apps stays. A pill with nothing in it (the Trash turned off) isn't drawn.
Full-width panel
A taskbar edge to edge, squared off against the screen's border, with no magnification.

Magnification, automatic hiding and the gap to the screen's edge work the same in Floating and Islands.

#Getting out of the way

Settings → Desktop & Dock → Dock → Hide the dock:

When a window needs the screen
The default. The dock keeps no strip of screen for itself: a maximized or fullscreen window uses the whole display, and the dock slides away while it does, instead of leaving a band of empty desktop around itself. Push the pointer to the screen's edge to bring it back for as long as you keep it there; it stays out while you use Launchpad or one of its own menus. A window that is merely open, or one you have moved and resized yourself, doesn't send it away.
Never
The dock always keeps its strip, and windows stop above it, as a taskbar does. The right choice for the full-width style.
Always
Hidden until the pointer reaches the edge, whatever is on screen.

#Settings

Settings → Desktop & Dock: position (bottom, left or right), the style above, icon size, magnification when pointing, when it gets out of the way, whether apps that are only open appear, and which apps are pinned. With magnification off, the icon under the pointer lights up instead. Desktop Profiles can change these together (Work, Gaming, Battery).
